what: As you scroll, images (photos, people, products) turn into a hologram from bottom to top — below the boundary, the grayscale image is tinted one color (--fx-holo) and sits under a translucent plate with thin scanlines every 4px, above it, the original image. An 18px light band sweeps along the boundary and number children count from 000 → 100. Progress runs over the first 95% of the span from when the section head is at 35% of the screen until the section end reaches the screen bottom (no curve — original hologram scan values)

options.span: Share of progress taken by the scan (0~1), default .95 — the rest stays fully changed
options.[data-fx-part=target]: (if present) picture to turn into a hologram — otherwise the first child. The motion part clones this and overlays it on top

use:
000

— Inside a long section, if you set the target up with position: sticky it gets scanned while pinned

from.where: scene.js hologram shader (person on a lab pedestal — original about timeline: section head top 35% → bottom bottom, progress 0→1 straight over .95, pedestal number panel 000→100). The site applies the shader to a 3D figure, while this motion part applies the same progress and the same look to a photo or DOM panel.

note: To paint the 3D object itself as a hologram, use the site’s shader (below the boundary height: edge light + scanlines + translucency). This part duplicates the image and overlays it, so it doesn’t suit video·canvas cells
